# Den Lennie Field Guides

> Straight answers on pricing, scope, positioning and growth for video production business owners. Den Lennie is an author and business coach for video production company owners, with three decades in production, more than a decade running his own production company, and eight years coaching owners through VBA (Video Business Accelerator). These field guides hold the questions video business owners actually ask, answered plainly.

## About

- [About Den Lennie](https://docs.denlennie.com/about-den-lennie): Author and coach for video business owners. Three decades in production, five books including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026), and VBA clients generating more than $52M in additional revenue over eight years.
- [What VBA offers](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-services): Coaching, community and tools for video production company owners. One programme, the VBA Elite Boardroom, plus the VBA AI toolset built for video production companies.
- [What VBA members say](https://docs.denlennie.com/vba-results): Results and testimonials from video business owners. $52M+ in additional revenue across members over eight years, in their own words.

## The S.C.A.L.E. Method and books

- [What is the S.C.A.L.E. Method?](https://docs.denlennie.com/scale-method): The framework from Den's 2026 book. Five disciplines a video business grows through: Survival, Control, Alignment, Leverage, Expansion.
- [The books Den Lennie has written](https://docs.denlennie.com/den-lennie-books): Five books for video business owners over more than a decade, including The S.C.A.L.E. Method (2026) and Business for Filmmakers (2014).

## Case studies

- [How a missing boundary cost a video business a client](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-revision-rounds): A video edit that blew past its agreed revision rounds and ended in a client walkout. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner stopped guessing on every quote](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-pricing-system): A hundred quotes in and still freezing on every one, until a real pricing method ended the anxiety. Anonymised.
- [How a video business owner escaped the project treadmill](https://docs.denlennie.com/case-study-recurring-revenue): Packaging existing work into a monthly retainer to move from one-off spikes to a rising floor. Anonymised.

## Pricing

- [What it costs to work with Den Lennie and VBA](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-guide): One programme, one price. The VBA Elite Boardroom is $1,700 USD a month, flat, cancel anytime. No onboarding fee, no minimum term, no application. Earlier programmes (Ascend, the Growth Strategy Session) are closed to new members.
- [How to price a video project so every quote isn't a guess](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-system): Day rate in four steps, the four-section quote, the ballpark script and what to say when a client pushes back, with a worksheet, quote skeleton and worked example to copy. Downloadable PDF.
- [Pricing Calculator: your day rate and a quote that holds](https://docs.denlennie.com/pricing-calculator): Floor and day rate from real overheads and sellable days, then a four-section quote with fee and contingency. Free, runs in the browser.
- [Charging for the invisible work: travel, delivery, storage, extras](https://docs.denlennie.com/charging-for-invisible-work): Travel, delivery, storage, extras: the work a video client never sees is the work owners give away for free. The four lines that belong on every quote, with the exact invoice wording: travel beyond 60 minutes each way, raw footage delivery, 12-month storage, and the extra half day on site. Plus the included-and-extra paragraph, a worked example and the rule. Downloadable PDF.
- [How many revision rounds to include, and how to charge for extra ones](https://docs.denlennie.com/revision-rounds): Two rounds of revisions per deliverable holds only if you define a round on the quote, count the rounds out loud at every delivery, and offer a choice before round three starts. The revision clause, a round definition, the scoreboard line, the pushback script, the price of an extra round and a worked example, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [The three revision emails, including the one for round three](https://docs.denlennie.com/revisions-field-guide): Three client email templates for revision rounds, led by the one to send when a client asks for changes after round two, plus what goes in the quote so they hold.
- [When a client's budget is lower than your quote, drop the scope, not the price](https://docs.denlennie.com/drop-scope-not-price): What to do when a client's budget is lower than your video quote: hold the rate, keep planning and filming, take deliverables and rounds out, and say it as a trade. The scope script, a three-option scope-down, the inclusions and exclusions wording, and a worked example, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [Why knowing your numbers lets you price with confidence](https://docs.denlennie.com/know-your-numbers): The three numbers every video business owner has to know: the floor a day must clear, the margin on each job built from crew at real day rates plus direct costs, and margin per day by client. A per-job margin worksheet, a monthly numbers review checklist, and the three-client example that shows why ranking clients by revenue gives the wrong answer. Downloadable PDF.

## Sales and clients

- [What to say when a prospect asks for a ballpark price](https://docs.denlennie.com/ballpark-price): What to say in the ten seconds after a prospect asks 'roughly how much?': give a range built the way you build a quote, make scope the variable, end with a question. The spoken script, the email reply, the line for 'can you just give me one number', and a worked example in round numbers. Downloadable PDF.
- [What to charge for video work: the pricing checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/price-checklist): What to charge for video work, and the six checks to run before any price leaves your mouth or your outbox: cost of a delivered day, a range for a ballpark, specific numbers, the whole job priced, four quote sections with contingency and a production company fee, and scope that moves while the price holds. A copy-and-paste checklist, a before-you-send routine and a worked example. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to get paid for everything you deliver: the scope checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/paid-checklist): Six checks that keep every piece of video work paid, a fill-in scope line for the quote (what's included, what's priced as an extra, what triggers a variation), and the script for the moment a client says "while you're here". All copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [The profitable quote checklist](https://docs.denlennie.com/quote-checklist): The pre-send checklist for a profitable video quote: three priced working sections, a 10 per cent contingency on the subtotal, a production company fee of 15 to 30 per cent on the production cost, inclusions stated, terms visible, one next step. Checklist, quote page skeleton and a worked example of a draft the checklist catches, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to qualify a video lead before you pitch](https://docs.denlennie.com/qualify-before-you-pitch): How to qualify a video lead before you quote: why sending the showreel and waiting loses, the five diagnostic questions for the first call, how to read fit, budget, decision-maker and timing, and a get-a-quote form with thank-you page wording. All copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to show real authority on a sales call](https://docs.denlennie.com/sales-call-authority): How to run a 30-minute discovery call with a video client: five questions that show authority, a summary back in their words, two or three options with their costs, and one dated next step. One-page call plan, summary-back line and options email, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to write a follow-up email that gets a reply](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-emails): How to write a follow-up email that gets a reply and how many times to follow up: add one useful thing, end on the next step, and keep to a cadence. Three emails, a cadence for your calendar or CRM, and next-step closers, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to push back on a client without losing them](https://docs.denlennie.com/push-back-without-losing-client): How to push back on a video client without losing them: why absorbing the cost teaches the wrong lesson, a five-step way to draw a line calmly, and copy-and-paste replies for extra work, late payment, a moved deadline, a fee cut after delivery, and raw footage that wasn't agreed. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to get more from referrals and networking](https://docs.denlennie.com/follow-up-referrals): Why warm introductions and networking contacts go cold, and how to stop it: following up an introduction or event contact within days, and asking a happy client for a referral without it being awkward. Four messages to copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.

## Marketing

- [Content or outreach: where to spend your marketing time](https://docs.denlennie.com/content-vs-outreach): Owners over-engineer content and under-execute outreach. Pick one channel, execute, adjust from data.
- [The marketing asset you already have and keep ignoring](https://docs.denlennie.com/use-what-you-have): Mine what you've already delivered before you commission the next shoot.
- [Feast or famine: why your video business swings, and the fix](https://docs.denlennie.com/feast-or-famine): The swings are the shape of your marketing. Market a little every week, busy or not.

## Positioning

- [How to choose a niche for your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/niche-paralysis): You don't have a lead problem, you have a 'who am I for' problem. How to find your niche in your last twelve months of jobs (margin, repeat, fit and proof), write it as a one-sentence niche-message-offer hypothesis, and test it with the people it describes before you touch your website. Job audit worksheet, hypothesis block and a test script, all copy and paste. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to use your own story to position your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/your-story-positioning): Your background is usually your strongest positioning asset, and most owners walk straight past it.

## Growth

- [How to move from one-off video projects to recurring revenue](https://docs.denlennie.com/recurring-revenue): One-off video work resets every month. How to turn a deliverable you already make into a monthly retainer: find the repeatable work, package it, price it in the house quote order, and propose it to an existing client. Retainer skeleton, the email, the line for "we don't need video every month", and a worked example in round numbers. Downloadable PDF.
- [How to grow revenue from the clients you already have](https://docs.denlennie.com/account-expansion): Account expansion is faster money than new logos, and most owners reach for the new logo first.
- [When one big client owns your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/one-client-dependency): A big anchor client is a gift and a risk. Audit your clients, then find more like the best one.

## Team

- [How to hire a video editor](https://docs.denlennie.com/hire-a-video-editor): Interview to filter, pay to decide. Never hire on the showreel alone.
- [Making your first hire in a video business: the fear, and the maths](https://docs.denlennie.com/first-hire): The fear is always the same: what if the work stops? Use your profit to buy your time back.

## Operations

- ["I need better systems in my business": where to actually start](https://docs.denlennie.com/better-systems): Better systems rarely means software. It means getting the business out of your head.

## Mindset

- [Handling the imposter feeling in your video business](https://docs.denlennie.com/imposter-syndrome): Many tactical questions owners ask are a proxy for reassurance. The answer is usually evidence, not another tactic.
- [Getting your weekends back as a video business owner](https://docs.denlennie.com/weekends-back): More revenue won't give you your weekends back. Build the business around the life.
